source.title: How Visual Representations Map to Language Feature Space in Multimodal LLMs
source.authors: Constantin Venhoff; Ashkan Khakzar; Sonia Joseph; P. Torr; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: The text has minor extraction garbling near the beginning and flattened figure content, but the paper is readable through its references.
record.tranche_reason: It extends SAE-based feature analysis to visual representations in a multimodal LLM and reports layer-wise results bearing on whether SAE features capture those representations.
record.gate_note: The benchmark scores in Table 1 evaluate the VLM, not feature superposition or SAE feature recovery, so they are not included as rows. SAE layer-wise plots are included; exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained GemmaScope SAEs as fixed probes and assumes they recover the LLM's features. It reports where projected visual tokens align with those language features across layers. Its results answer a cross-modal alignment question. They do not bear on whether LLMs store sparse, SAE-recoverable features (V4) or on any other version, since SAE quality on text is only used as the comparison reference.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say visual representations are 'fully mapped onto LLM features' around layer 18 and misaligned earlier. They frame this as possible evidence that adapter-based architectures align poorly with early LLM layers.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a test of the original toy-network superposition method. It trains a linear adapter between frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 and Gemma-2-2b-it, then uses pretrained GemmaScope SAEs to analyze visual-token representations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported alignment varies by layer: the authors identify middle-to-late layers, around layer 18 of 26, as the convergence region and describe earlier layers as misaligned.

fits_no_version.finding: In a frozen CLIP–Gemma-2-2B-it VLM, SAE reconstruction error, sparsity and GPT-4o-judged feature-description match for image tokens converge toward text-token levels around layer 18 of 26. Image tokens are misaligned in earlier layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearly projected visual tokens become expressible in a frozen LLM's SAE feature basis only in middle-to-late layers.

record.problems: Evidence is from one VLM configuration with frozen backbones. The plotted layer-wise values are not numerically transcribed in the text, no uncertainty estimates are reported, and the semantic feature-description matching is judged by GPT-4o.

untested.parts: All parts; no capacity or importance analysis.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs. The study assumes this and uses GemmaScope as a probe.

record.verdict_notes: The study is a short workshop-style paper with figure-only results, no uncertainty estimates, and a single model. Its SAE measures serve as alignment probes. The record's 'baseline not stated' is wrong: text-only examples are the stated baseline.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, feature overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or importance.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The study tests SAE-feature alignment for visual representations in one frozen-backbone VLM; it does not test how generally LLM features are distributed across neurons or other models and settings.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.
